subject: Post-call: Buying flow owners, contract sequencing & redline turn-times
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@healthgrid.io>, Tom Baker <tom.baker@healthgrid.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap + owners for next steps (NDA / MSA / DPA sequencing)

Hi Claire / Tom — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth: 

Summary of what we heard
- Primary use case: embed LLM-based clinical note summarization and triage for patient intake flows (pilot scope: 3 clinics).
- Key decision criteria: data locality & audit logs, predictable per-token economics, and SLA for 99.9% uptime during business hours.
- Timeline: procurement + legal review target before end of August to kick off a September pilot.

Proposed owners & routing
- Economic buyer: Claire Nguyen (confirmed) — responsible for final approval and budget sign-off.
- Security / compliance: Tom Baker to coordinate SOC 2 evidence and data flow diagrams with your security team.
- Procurement / legal: Procurement Team (procurement@healthgrid.io) will handle the NDA and MSA review; they asked for typical turn-times so we propose the sequence below.

Suggested contract sequencing and SLAs for turn-times
1) Mutual NDA (to cover initial sharing of test data) — target turnaround: 3 business days for signature once we send draft.
2) Data Processing Addendum (DPA) comms — run in parallel with NDA redlines, target 5 business days to agree on standard clauses.
3) Master Service Agreement (MSA) — initiated after mutual terms are aligned; aim for a 7–10 business day redline window for initial round, then 2–3 business days for exec sign-off once MSA redlines are agreed.

Actions I can take this week
- Share our mutual NDA draft and a simple project scope (attached).
- Push an internal MSA sequencing recommendation to help accelerate procurement.

Ask from you
- Confirm economic approver (I have Claire) and the preferred contract contact for legal redlines (name + email).
- If procurement prefers a different sequencing (e.g., MSA first), flag now and we'll adapt.

Attachments: HealthGrid_NDA_v1.pdf (sample NDA), MAG-POC-scope.docx

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a short mutual action plan doc and a proposed calendar for reviews.

—
Jasmine Liu
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
jasmine.liu@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0132

From: Claire Nguyen <claire.nguyen@healthgrid.io>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Baker <tom.baker@healthgrid.io>, Procurement Team <procurement@healthgrid.io>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + owners for next steps (NDA / MSA / DPA sequencing)

Thanks, Jasmine — this is helpful and aligned to what we discussed. A few notes from our side: 

- Confirmed: I’m the economic approver and will own budget sign-off.
- Procurement contact for formal redlines: Anika Shah (anika.shah@healthgrid.io) — she’ll take point on the NDA/MSA routing.
- Security wants the SOC 2 Type II report and an architecture diagram showing encryption at rest/in transit. Tom will send the architecture artifact by end of day.

Sequencing preference
We’d prefer: NDA first (fast), DPA in parallel, and MSA afterwards. If we can get NDA signed and DPA draft agreed by 08/05, we can put procurement on an expedited track for the MSA. 

Also: Procurement asked whether you can share a proposed signer ladder — who at Redwood needs to approve the MSA and who executes signature (people + titles). That will help speed internal routing on our side.

Thanks again — looping in Anika.

Best,
Claire
VP, Product & Partnerships | HealthGrid
claire.nguyen@healthgrid.io

What I need from you: 
- Marissa: can you provide the recommended signer ladder (names, titles, who is required for signature vs approval) and whether we can commit to the 7–10 business day initial redline window?
- Ben / Neha: please confirm whether we should send the NDA v1 as-is or pre-redline a few MSA terms (liability cap, data residency) to avoid iterative rounds. Procurement signaled that parallelizing a handful of MSA non-negotiables with the NDA would shave off time.

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Jul 2027 15:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Post-call recap + owners — need redline sequencing & signer ladder from Legal/RevOps

Thanks for the ping, Jasmine. Quick answers below so you can reply to Anika/Procurement and lock calendar slots: 

Signer ladder (Redwood) — who signs and who approves
- Legal review / redlines: Marissa Cole, Head of Contracts (marissa.cole@redwood.ai) — owns legal redline responses and escalation for non-standard terms.
- Commercial approval (limits on concessions / discounts): Ben Carter, Sr. AE (ben.carter@redwood.ai) — required if discounting beyond playbook.
- Executive signatory (final signature): Vivek Kulkarni, COO (vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai) — signs MSA for enterprise deals > $250k ARR. For pilot/POC under that threshold, I can sign as Head of Contracts.

Turn-times and sequencing commitments
- NDA: we will send a signed mutual NDA within 2 business days of receiving Anika’s finalized contact details — aim to complete signature within 3 business days.
- DPA: we will provide a draft DPA alongside the NDA and can accept 4–6 business days for negotiation on standard terms; if HealthGrid needs custom clauses, escalate to me directly.
- MSA: Redwood Legal prefers single redline file (native Word with tracked changes) for the first round. We can commit to a 7–10 business day turnaround for the initial redline round from receipt. If there are only minor points, we’ll compress to 3–4 business days.

Pre-redline suggestions
- To speed procurement, go ahead and include the following MSA items in parallel: liability cap, data residency clause, and termination for convenience notice. We’ll pre-populate recommended language before Anika opens redlines.

I’ll prepare the signer ladder and example redline policy doc and drop into the shared Drive link by Monday morning. Ben — can you prepare a short note on commercial flexibility (discount thresholds) so procurement has clarity?

—
Marissa Cole
Head of Contracts | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0199
